stat_facts: Increases health and reduces chance to be dazed in combat (wiki Statistics; '1 STA = 1 HP' is marked 'need testing' there).
Increases melee and ranged weapon damage and shield block amounts; 1 STR = 2 weight (wiki Statistics).
Increases hit rate, weapon proc frequency and gives a channeling bonus to spellcasters (wiki Statistics).
Mana pool size if INT is higher than WIS, and offensive spell damage (wiki Statistics).
Mana pool size if WIS is higher than INT, and healing done; 4 mana per WIS point for WIS-based classes (wiki Statistics).
Merchant prices and charm break rate on paper; the wiki notes CHA did not seem to affect vendor prices in beta (May 2026).

mana.text: Your mana stat is whichever of INT or WIS is higher (wiki Statistics); 93 of 127 wiki Necromancer spells cost mana.
mana.label: FACT

wiki_advice: Below is the recommended allocation of bonus points by race. Since Intelligence is a Necromancer’s main attribute, you should focus on maximizing it whenever possible. Your spell damage and mana total is directly tied to it. After that, prioritize Stamina. It gives you extra HP and a bit of stun resistance. Finally, put a point or two into Dexterity. It affects hit rate across the board and increases your proc chance. Gnome: +4 Stamina, +1 Dexterity, and +5 Intelligence Goblin: +3 Stamina, +1 Dexterity, and +6 Intelligence Human: +2 Stamina, +1 Dexterity, and +7 Intelligence

traits.why: Intelligent: +5% INT and a 15-second +50% INT burst.
Alteration (51) and Conjuration (41) are the two biggest Necromancer schools on the wiki.
Readiness gives a Cantrip slot from level 1, so one memorized spell survives death.

Miner starts Mining at 25 with a Trainee's Mining Pick and Pouch, matching the default gathering setup (Mining, Lumberjacking, Smelting) for early coin. Medic (Bind Wound 25 and bandages) is the safer pick if you expect downtime between fights. Blacksmith exists but smithing stays off by default here.
